title: Round, Then Add or Subtract
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Use the pattern from the lesson in your head before you type. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: Estimate $[[a]] + [[b]]$ by rounding each number to the nearest ten first.
hints: Round $[[a]]$ and $[[b]]$ to the nearest ten.
Add the rounded numbers.

problems.prompt: Estimate $[[10*m]] + [[10*n]]$ by rounding each number to the nearest hundred first.
hints: Round each number to the nearest hundred: look at the tens digit.

problems.prompt: Estimate $[[10*m]] - [[10*n]]$ by rounding each number to the nearest hundred first.
hints: Round both numbers to the nearest hundred, then subtract.

problems.prompt: On a trip there are $[[a]]$ pupils and $[[b]]$ adults. Round each number to the nearest ten. About how many people are on the trip?
hints: Round each number to the nearest ten, then add.

problems.prompt: Work out $[[a]] + [[b]]$ exactly, and estimate it by rounding each number to the nearest ten. How far apart are the two answers?
hints: How far did each number move when you rounded it?
Combine the two moves.
problems.solution: Exact: $[[a+b]]$. Estimate: $[[10*floor((a+5)/10) + 10*floor((b+5)/10)]]$. They are $[[abs(a + b - 10*floor((a+5)/10) - 10*floor((b+5)/10))]]$ apart.

title: Friendly Numbers for Division
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Use the pattern from the lesson in your head before you type. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: Estimate $[[a*k+r]] \div [[k]]$ by using the nearby multiple $[[a*k]]$.
hints: $[[a*k]]$ is in the $[[k]]$ times table. Which fact?

problems.prompt: Estimate $[[10*a*k + r]] \div [[k]]$ by using a friendly number from the $[[k]]$ times table.
hints: Find a multiple of $[[k]]$ close to $[[10*a*k+r]]$ that ends in $0$.

problems.prompt: How many whole times does $[[k]]$ go into $[[a*k+r]]$?
hints: Find the biggest multiple of $[[k]]$ that is not more than $[[a*k+r]]$.
problems.solution: $[[k]] \times [[a]] = [[a*k]]$ and $[[k]] \times [[a+1]] = [[(a+1)*k]]$ is too big, so $[[a]]$ times, with $[[r]]$ left over.

problems.prompt: Work out $[[a*k*10]] \div [[k]]$.
hints: Use the fact $[[a*k]] \div [[k]] = [[a]]$.

problems.prompt: $[[a*k+r]]$ pupils go on a trip in minibuses that seat $[[k]]$. How many minibuses are needed?

mistakes.why: That leaves $[[r]]$ pupils without a seat. They need one more bus.

hints: How many full buses? How many pupils are left over?
problems.solution: $[[k]] \times [[a]] = [[a*k]]$ seats $[[a*k]]$ pupils, and $[[r]]$ are left. They need one more bus: $[[a+1]]$.

title: Is the Answer Sensible?
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Use the pattern from the lesson in your head before you type. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: What is the last digit of $[[a]] \times [[b]]$?
hints: Multiply just the last digits.
problems.solution: Only the last digits decide: $[[mod(a,10)]] \times [[mod(b,10)]] = [[mod(a,10)*mod(b,10)]]$, which ends in $[[mod(mod(a,10)*mod(b,10),10)]]$.

problems.prompt: What is the last digit of $[[a]] + [[b]] + [[c]]$?
hints: Add just the last digits.
problems.solution: Add the last digits: $[[mod(a,10)]] + [[mod(b,10)]] + [[mod(c,10)]] = [[mod(a,10)+mod(b,10)+mod(c,10)]]$, which ends in $[[mod(mod(a,10)+mod(b,10)+mod(c,10),10)]]$.

problems.prompt: Ella says $[[a]] \times [[k]] = [[10*a*k]]$. Estimate to find her mistake. What is the right answer?
hints: Estimate the product first.
Then work it out exactly by splitting $[[a]]$ into tens and ones.
problems.solution: Estimate: about $[[10*floor((a+5)/10)*k]]$. Her answer is ten times too big. The right answer is $[[a*k]]$.

problems.prompt: Tom works out $[[a*k]] \div [[k]]$ and gets $[[10*a]]$. Estimate to check. What is the right answer?
hints: Multiply Tom’s answer by $[[k]]$: do you get $[[a*k]]$?
problems.solution: $[[k]] \times [[10*a]] = [[10*a*k]]$, which is ten times $[[a*k]]$. The right answer is $[[a]]$.

problems.prompt: Estimate $[[a]] \times [[b]]$ by rounding both to the nearest ten. Then work out the exact answer. Type the exact answer.
hints: Split one number into tens and ones to work it out exactly.
Check your answer is close to the estimate.
problems.solution: Estimate: $[[10*floor((a+5)/10)]] \times [[10*floor((b+5)/10)]] = [[100*floor((a+5)/10)*floor((b+5)/10)]]$. Exact: $[[a*b]]$, close to the estimate.
